item.content:encoded:
Brandon Valenzuela began the 2026 season as catching depth, but when the season was over he had seemingly solidified himself as the backup catcher for the foreseeable future for the Toronto Blue Jays. What looked like a temporary promotion after Alejandro Kirk fractured his left thumb became a season-long audition in which Valenzuela established himself as an elite defender. He even earned recognition as an American League Gold Glove finalist.
That depth is valuable, but it also brings up a legitimate offseason question. With Kirk entrenched as the starter, would the Blue Jays be better served keeping Valenzuela as a high-end backup or using his rising value to address a more pressing need elsewhere on the roster?
Why Valenzuela has real trade value
Valenzuela’s market starts with his defense. In 91 games as a rookie, he ranked among the top five major-league catchers in Statcast Fielding Run Value and FanGraphs’ defensive rating. His framing and blocking gave Toronto’s pitchers a steady target, while his arm helped him throw out 19 of 63 attempted base stealers.
He also held his own at the plate for the first half of the season when he produced a .241/.322/.407 line and a 106 wRC+. Valenzuela’s age and years of club control would certainly be intriguing for prospective teams. Getting a 26-year-old catcher who has already shown he can handle a major-league staff is the type of profile that could be the centre of a decent trade package.
However, there will be detractors around the league. While Valenzuela finished with nine home runs, a double-digit walk rate and a .688 OPS across 271 plate appearances, his second half numbers were not good. He produced a .182/.276/.299 with a 65 wRC+ after the All-Star break. His walk rate held steady, but the strikeouts started to tick up and and he hit just two home runs.
To be fair, rookie catchers often wear down under the physical and mental demands of the position, and teams will likely value his defence first. But it does, limit the return Toronto can reasonably expect. Valenzuela alone is unlikely to fetch an established middle-of-the-order bat or a frontline starter. A more realistic outcome would be a need-for-need deal involving a player with similar control and upside.
What could the Blue Jays get on the trade market for Brandon Valenzuela?
There are several teams that are likely looking for a catcher this offseason and the free agent market is somewhat thin. Three teams that could meet a need-for-need trade are the New York Yankees, Chicago Cubs and Cincinnati Reds.
Yankees - Luis Garcia Jr.
The most ambitious idea would be a deal with the Yankees centred on Luis García Jr. García hit 30 home runs with an .830 OPS in 2026, although his production slipped to a .264/.302/.434 slash line after New York acquired him at the deadline but they are already rumored to be shopping around Garcia this offseason.
His left-handed power would interest Toronto, and returning Garcia back to second base while filling in for Guerrero Jr. at first could address the need to get more pop from the right side of the infield.
The Yankees would almost certainly demand more than Valenzuela in return. But they are also desperate to upgrade on Austin Wells behind the dish and they will need to potentially replace other players such as Trent Grisham, Jazz Chisholm, David Bednar, and Paul Goldschmidt just to name a few.
Cubs - Kevin Alcántara
Chicago is potentially losing Carson Kelly behind the plate, putting the Cubs in need of a replacement. Kevin Alcántara is a 24-year-old right-handed outfielder that will be fighting for playing time with the South Siders. Alcántara hit 20 home runs with an .852 OPS at Triple-A in 2026.
The power and handedness should intrigue Toronto who currently only has two MLB outfielders who bat from the right side and that's Anthony Santander (a switch-hitter and outfielder is a loose term with him) and Davis Schenider (who could be a non-tender candidate).
It could be risky to move a proven MLB backup catcher (at worst) in Valenzuela for Alcántara who has yet to stick around in the big leagues after 37 games over three stints dating back to 2024. But the Blue Jays need some flexibility in their outfield corps and after the Blue Jays had so much success with their last trade with the Cubs they might be wise to go to the well again.
Reds - JJ Bleday
JJ Bleday represents another version of the same need-for-need framework. The Cincinnati outfielder hit .217/.324/.416 with 24 home runs and 72 walks in 2026. Again, the pop is the selling point here and he's under team control through 2028.
His significant second-half drop and stronger production against right-handed pitching make him more of a platoon-oriented corner bat and, as stated, the Blue Jays already have a few of those in Nathan Lukes, Addison Barger, Sean Keys and Yohendrick Piñango. Still, if Cincinnati decides it needs a defensive upgrade behind the plate, Valenzuela could form the foundation of a conversation.
Keeping Valenzuela may still be the better move
The strongest argument against a trade is Kirk’s 2026 injury. Toronto learned how quickly catching depth can derail a season. Valenzuela helped stabilize a key piece of the Blue Jays roster and held his own.
There is also room for both catchers. Kirk is the clear starter, but carrying Valenzuela would allow Toronto to protect him from overuse and they could use either catcher at designated hitter on occasion
Valenzuela has enough value that the Blue Jays should not make him untouchable, and if another club is willing to exchange a controllable everyday outfielder, or a credible second-base option, Toronto would be justified in using its catching depth to improve a thinner area of the roster.
But dealing him simply because Kirk is ahead of him would be a mistake. Valenzuela’s defence, affordability and ability to step into a larger role give the Blue Jays more certainty than most teams possess behind their starting catcher. Unless the return clearly improves the 2027 roster, keeping one of baseball’s better defensive catching tandems is the safer—and probably smarter—choice.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Phillies Boss Pinpoints ‘Really, Really Good’ Infield Replacement After Trea Turner Decision
item.dc:creator: Peter Chawaga; Contributor
item.description: The Philadelphia Phillies head into yet another offseason with questions to answer about their roster construction after an early postseason exit. Earlier this week, during his end of season press conference, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski made it clear that the team needs to improve defensively, and one of its biggest decisions could involve a veteran who remains central to the franchise. "From a defensive perspective, we are very clear," Dombrowski said of Trea Turner, accord
item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies head into yet another offseason with questions to answer about their roster construction after an early postseason exit.
Earlier this week, during his end of season press conference, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski made it clear that the team needs to improve defensively, and one of its biggest decisions could involve a veteran who remains central to the franchise.
"From a defensive perspective, we are very clear," Dombrowski said of Trea Turner, according to the New York Post's Matt Ehalt. "He knows he has to be better at shortstop. And I told him that it's really mandatory that he's like that."
Though Dombrowski made it clear that Turner no longer has a lock on the shortstop position, the Phillies seem reliant on the long-term contracts already on the books, including his. But during the same press conference, the front office boss singled out one new player who could join the roster next season.
Philadelphia Phillies Boss Highlights Trea Turner Replacement After Harsh Warning
If Turner cannot return to his previous defensive form, Dombrowski made it clear that he will consider other options. Initially, it seems most likely that the team would shift Turner to second base or to the outfield and move Bryson Stott to shortstop.
But the Phillies president also pinpointed an exciting young infielder as an example of a new player who could join the mix next season.
"I'm not going to put it on his back, but we think a guy like Aidan Miller is a really, really good player," Dombrowski said, according to MLB.com's Todd Zolecki. "You see all the young players that have jumped into playing this year and the years that they had. Aidan Miller, when he's healthy, he's as good as any of them."
Turner is entering the fourth season of his 11-year, $300 million contract, and the Phillies have not ruled out keeping him at shortstop. But Dombrowski singled out Miller as an intriguing option to take some pressure off of the team's veteran core of position players, and it seems that if and when he does receive a promotion, he could be taking over the shortstop role.
Philadelphia Phillies' Trea Turner Replacement Could Already Be In The Organization
Miller's potential makes him an interesting name to watch as the Phillies consider their infield options, although his arrival should not be viewed as a certainty for Opening Day.
The prospect entered 2026 as Philadelphia's top-ranked position prospect but lost much of the season to a back injury that required surgery in June. He returned to action in September, appearing in four regular-season games across the Florida Complex League and Double-A Reading before helping Reading during its Eastern League championship run.
For now, Turner has an opportunity to retain his position by improving defensively. But with Dombrowski publicly identifying Miller as a potential contributor, the Phillies have another avenue to explore if their veteran shortstop cannot deliver the necessary improvement.
This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: [inquirer.com] Sorry, Phillies fans, Dave Dombrowski is not going anywhere | Marcus Hayes
item.dc:creator: Marcus Hayes

If you’re a Dave Dombrowski hater, no matter where you were or what you were doing, your blood ran cold Thursday morning. That was when the Phillies president of baseball operations
item.content:encoded:
Skip to content
Sorry, Phillies fans, Dave Dombrowski is not going anywhere for a long, long time. Is that a bad thing?
Dealin' Dave, President for Life, denied offering a job to Alex Cora, said Trea Turner must audition at shortstop, and said the farm system is A-OK. Seriously: I hope John Middleton never fires him.
If you’re a Dave Dombrowski hater, no matter where you were or what you were doing, your blood ran cold Thursday morning. That was when the Phillies president of baseball operations, in his post-season news conference, blithely remarked:
“I plan on being here for a while. I enjoy it. I’m healthy. I have quality people around me.”
In a town whose football team has lost three straight and whose coach blew the last game in the last 8 seconds; whose basketball team hasn’t gotten past the second round of the playoffs in 25 years; and whose hockey team is winless in its first nine games, Dombrowski is, by far, the most despised sports figure.
And he’s here for the long haul.
Marcus Hayes alerts
During his 61-minute, end-of-season news conference, Dombrowski addressed important issues: Trea Turner’s pending and overdue removal from the shortstop position; his unwillingness to trade from among the starting pitching but his willingness to trade star hitters if those hitters were willing; announcements that Don Mattingly will return as manager and turnover on the coaching staff; and his faith in a minor-league system that he believes is incorrectly rated among the worst in baseball.
But his own future, both long- and short-term, was the most significant issue of the day.
Is that a bad thing? Most Phillies fans, in this moment, would answer, resoundingly, “Yes.”
The backstory
Dombrowski took the Phillies to the World Series in 2022, his second season, but playoff collapses in the following four seasons authored mainly by Dombrowski’s porous bullpens and choking hitters put a target on his back that even José Alvarado could hit. This year, as the Phillies faded from the top wild-card slot to the final wild-card slot to a three-game wild-card exit in Atlanta, Dombrowski’s star sank lower than ever in every corner of Philadelphia ... except one. It’s the only corner that matters.
It’s the office of John Middleton, the Phillies’ managing partner.
Middleton adores Dombrowski. Last month, following up a report by The Athletic that Dombrowski will soon receive an extension beyond his current deal’s expiration in 2027, I was told by a Phillies source, “Middleton will never fire Dombrowski.”
» READ MORE: Don Mattingly ‘carried the stick.’ That helped make him the best choice as Phillies manager.
A few days later, USA Today reported that the Phillies will offer Dombrowski a lifetime contract, presumably to fill whatever role he desires. Right now, at the age of 70, he still desires to decide who’s on the roster and who’s managing them.
Has he earned it? Not in Philadelphia, no. But elsewhere, Dombrowski won two World Series and went to two more. Middleton adores him; essentially, in Middleton’s eyes, Dombrowski can do no wrong.
In my eyes, Dombrowski’s been about average. He inherited an organization that included Bryce Harper, Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sánchez, Aaron Nola, J.T. Realmuto, Alec Bohm, and Bryson Stott.
He’s extended some of those deals, signed Kyle Schwarber (twice), enhanced the roster with trades for Jesús Luzardo and Jhoan Duran, and hit on deadline deals for Harrison Bader in 2025 and Luis Arraez in 2026 (both were hurt in the playoffs, though).
He also has consistently failed to replace the right-handed power of Rhys Hoskins, has shown abominable judgment in bullpen construction, and, in seeking optimal offensive output, has inexcusably and illogically devalued defense, especially for a team so heavily invested in big-money starting pitching: He has four $100 million starters.
Further, the contracts of outfielder Nick Castellanos, a defensive liability, Turner, a defensive liability, and starter Taijuan Walker, the ultimate defensive liability, proved utterly indefensible.
Still, as Middleton loves to point out, any president who takes a team to the playoffs five years in a row must be doing something right.
» READ MORE: To Dave Dombrowski, the Phillies’ problems begin an arm’s length away
Counterpoint: In Dombrowski’s case, so far, most of what he’s done right is that he hasn’t messed with what former GM Matt Klentak left him.
Also: If the Phillies are such a quality team with such a bright future, why did Alex Cora, the manager who won Dombrowski the 2018 World Series in Boston, turn down the manager’s job twice in six months? Does he want to win Puerto Rico the Father of the Year this badly?
Furthermore, if Dombrowski was such a hotshot executive, why did the Sox fire him less than 11 months after winning it all?
None of those questions matter. What matters is, John hearts Dave.
Madness ensues
I, for one, am happy that Dombrowski is sticking around. That’s mainly because I, for one, don’t care if the Phillies win every game, lose every game, or have every game rained out, as long as they’re interesting while doing it.
Also, I enjoy talking to Dombrowski. He’s smart, intriguing, and his hair has its own aura, as the kids say.
Besides, how can I endorse firing a guy who I’m giving a grade like “C?” You know, average. You fire guys who get D’s and F’s.
That “C” grade means Dombrowski probably does a better job at roster building than, say, I, who am a connoisseur of shortstops (and point guards); a far better job than, say Mike Sielski, whose expertise is limited to hockey centermen; but probably not as good a job as David Murphy, who obsesses on wRC+ and FIP (and who, incongruently, is a quarterback aficionado, too).
» READ MORE: Phillies will keep Trea Turner at shortstop for now: ‘He knows he has to be better’
Also, Dombrowski says crazy stuff.
He fired Rob Thomson and, after being turned down by Cora, the fired former Red Sox manager, he replaced Thomson with Mattingly, the bench coach, as interim manager.
Dombrowski said Thursday that, while he’d followed a baseball mandate and interviewed other candidates, he had never offered the job to anyone but Mattingly. He said this with a straight face ... after both USA Today and the Phillies’ own website reported that, early last week, Cora had turned him down again.
Dombrowski on Thursday also said he actually signed Mattingly to a deal last Saturday, but, with the Eagles playing Sunday (24 hours later) and with Mattingly lacking solid internet service at his vacation lodgings, they delayed leaking the news until Wednesday ... so as to have better Wi-Fi on Thursday for Mattingly’s Zoom news conference.
I am not making any of that up.
Old MacDonald’s farm
Dombrowski also tried to convince listeners that their farm system is better than the experts rank it, which is generally between fifth-to-last and second-to-last. He asserted that major league rookies Andrew Painter, Justin Crawford, and Alex McFarlane should count toward their farm depth, and that they should be credited for using prospects to acquire Luzardo and Duran.
Dombrowski ignored the fact that Painter and Crawford did not factor into the current rankings at all, and he ignored the fact that teams ranked higher than his also traded prospects to improve. For instance, the Dodgers traded three prospects at the deadline to acquire Tarik Skubal from the Tigers, two of them ranked in the top 100 by MLB.com, and still had an elite system at the season’s end. The Brewers also traded prospects for bullpen help at the deadline, and their farm system remains as good or better than the Dodgers’ — whom they just swept out of the NLCS.
Coup de grace
The nuttiest thing Dombrowski said in his hourlong State of the Union regarded Turner. By most metrics, Turner was, by far, the worst defensive shortstop in all of baseball. Dombrowski’s solution:
He forced Turner to leave his home in Florida and travel to Philadelphia for a two-hour meeting with Dombrowski, which is like a kid on summer break getting called back to school to go to the principal’s office. What did they talk about for two hours? Some of it concerned Turner’s career-worst offensive performance, which is weird, since that’s kind of the job of the manager and the hitting coach. Some of it concerned Turner’s defense.
Dombrowski warned Turner that Turner would have to audition in spring training if he hopes to retain the shortstop job. Otherwise, he will be moved, most likely to left field, though Turner would prefer staying on the infield, most likely at second base.
» READ MORE: The most imaginative changes the Phillies can make begin with moving Trea Turner off shortstop
What?
WHAT?
So, the plan to return the 33-year-old’s defensive skills from putridity back to their heights, which were mediocrity, is to have him walk on eggshells for 20 spring training games? In which he will play, what, a total of 90 innings — 90 innings that Turner could spend acclimating himself to second base, where he’s started just 79 games, or left field where he’s played zero games?
Assume Turner exits spring training as the shortstop, then he commits four errors in April — again. Do you banish him to the grass or push him to the right side of the infield in the middle of the season? What chance does he have to succeed in that sort of atmosphere?
Of all the harebrained schemes the Phillies have hatched in the past 15 years or so, the plan for Turner is the wildest. Really, this stuff just writes itself. Thanks, Dave.
And, Mr. Middleton: To hell with your fans. For my sake, and for the sake of columnists everywhere, please never fire Dave Dombrowski.

item.title: [puckettspond.com] This year's World Series shows where the Twins have failed
item.dc:creator: Chris Schad
item.description: The Minnesota Twins have spent another October watching the postseason from home and the biggest question is why. item.content:encoded:
The Minnesota Twins have spent another October watching the postseason from home and the biggest question is why. The Twins have missed the playoffs in five of the past six seasons and while many are rightfully upset about the team’s payroll slashing, there are also several fundamental mistakes that have prevented them from being successful.
Those mistakes will be front and center during this year’s World Series. The Milwaukee Brewers punched their ticket to the Fall Classic after completing a sweep over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night and they will face either the Tampa Bay Rays or Cleveland Guardians in what will be a showdown between small-market teams.
While this year’s matchup could create a loophole for the Pohlad family to avoid dropping a large amount of money to improve the team, it also reflects poorly on their decisions that have kept them from competing over the past few years.
The Brewers, Rays and Guardians are showing the Twins how to build a winner
As you may have guessed, the Brewers, Guardians and Rays are not among MLB’s biggest spenders. According to Cot’s Baseball Contracts, the Brewers’ year-end salary ranked 23rd at $99.3 million and defeated the Dodgers’ No. 1 roster at $366.0 million. The American League finalists were also budget-conscious as the Rays ranked 20th with a year-end payroll of $103.1 million and the Guardians ranked 25th at $91.0 million.
All three of the remaining teams had a lower year-end payroll than the Twins, who ranked 17th with a figure of $123.9 million and while many, including owner and chairman Tom Pohlad, believe that adding to that number could lead to a championship, the other three teams show what they have done wrong.
The first is maximizing the value of players on the roster. The Rays, Guardians and Brewers have traded players before they get to free agency to add to their organization and it’s paid off in a big way. The Brewers most notably did this in a February 2024 trade featuring Corbin Burnes that brought back left-hander DL Hall and infielder Joey Ortiz.
The Rays also have done this with their trade of Triple-A right-hander Tobias Myers, who was traded to Cleveland as he was eligible for the Rule 5 Draft in 2021, and brought back star third baseman Junior Caminero in return. While the Guardians whiffed on Myers, they made other shrewd deals that netted them Craig Yoho, Patrick Bailey, Foster Griffin and Kyle Manzardo.
These trades are a double-edged sword as they usually involve popular players. But it brings back pieces that ensure a larger championship window. That leaves player development as the final phase of the three contenders and each team has a homegrown star to lean on such as Jose Ramirez, Jacob Misiorowski or Caminero.
The Twins’ biggest problems go beyond their payroll
Turning the attention back to the Twins, it’s easy to see where they have come up short. This year’s trade deadline was one opportunity to shift the narrative. But instead of trading players that could bring back a big return such as Ryan Jeffers and Joe Ryan, the Twins went the opposite direction, adding A.J. Minter, Jeff Hoffman and Dean Kremer.
Even when they tried to trade Trevor Larnach to the Houston Astros before owner Jim Crane vetoed it, they were seeking 29-year-old Bryan Abreu, a pitcher who posted his highest ERA (3.73) and lowest WAR (1.0) since his rookie season in 2021.
The other key issue is the Twins’ player development. While top prospects such as Royce Lewis and Matt Wallner thrive initially when reaching the major leagues, those players have hit a wall when pitchers adjust to them. The problem can be traced back to Miguel Sano’s downfall in the early 2020s and can still be seen in a group of post-hype hitters that haven’t lived up to their prospect status.
This leaves the Twins in a tricky spot this offseason. After failing to trade Jeffers at the deadline, there’s a good chance he’ll leave in free agency. Ryan has a year of team control remaining, but trading him now could get a pair of MLB-ready players in return. Several top prospects including Walker Jenkins, Emmanuel Rodriguez and Kaelen Culpepper made their debuts this season, but the key will be to make sure they don’t regress entering their first full season in the bigs.
Of course, fans may cheer for a salary floor to hold the Pohlads accountable for what happens to the Twins next. But the Rays, Guardians and Brewers show that paying top dollar may not be necessary to build a contender and Minnesota would be wise to follow their blueprint.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox should finally capitalize as insider confirms Padres-Jarren Duran trade interest
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli

item.content:encoded:
After two seasons that ended in the same Wild Card elimination by the same team in the same stadium, upgrading the offense should be the Boston Red Sox's No. 1 priority. There's so much depth in their lineup that there isn't an exceedingly obvious place to add, but it's long been established that their outfield group needs to be shrunk.
Following a career-worst season during which he was one of the worst qualified hitters in the league, trading Jarren Duran seems like an easy answer. Finding a suitor for him after a severe offensive regression and multiple instances of off-the-field drama won't be easy, however.
But MLB insider Jon Heyman reports there's still interest in Duran from one team — the one we all expect. Heyman said in his Bleacher Report live stream that the San Diego Padres are still interested in the outfielder.
The Friars have long expressed their desire to trade for Duran. They've publicly been the team most interested in dealing for him, though there could be others behind the scenes. San Diego once offered Boston Dylan Cease, top catching prospect Ethan Salas and one other prospect for Duran, which the Red Sox "quickly rejected," according to Sean McAdam of MassLive.
MLB insider Jon Heyman says Padres are still interested in Jarren Duran trade with Red Sox
Cease would've just been a rental, but the Red Sox should've taken that deal. They could've extended Cease, but Duran's value was never going to increase — time is ticking down on his contract and he had never shown that he could maintain the level of offensive production he had in 2024, when he earned the All-Star Game MVP and came in eighth in American League MVP voting.
The Padres are likely to lose outfielders Miguel Andujar, Austin Hays and Ramón Laureano to the free agent market, meaning they could use another body in their pastures. Duran's .207/.266/.361 slash line and 165 strikeouts over 151 games are hardly encouraging, but he's a prime change-of-scenery candidate and he could rebound elsewhere.
Boston must prioritize trading Duran (and Masataka Yoshida) not only to give it lineup flexibility, but to open its designated hitter spot for a power bat rather than maintaining the rotating DH structure that it's gone with in recent years. The Red Sox need their top hitters in the lineup every day, and signing or trading for someone who could swap between DH and left field with Roman Anthony is seemingly the easiest way to add power to the lineup.
Trading Duran is also the optimal outcome this offseason because he's regressed so severely that he could be a non-tender risk. At least trading him to the Padres would net the Red Sox a return, however small.
The Red Sox need to clear their outfield logjam if they're serious about improving their offense. Trading Duran should be the first step to their upswing.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Rays Need Junior Caminero to Wake Up Before It's Too Late
item.dc:creator: Christian Rauh
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays are now facing a difficult situation in the American League Championship Series after falling 3-2 to the Cleveland Guardians in Game 3 on Thursday. And while there are plenty of things to criticize about the performance, I think the biggest concern continues to be the lack of offensive production from Tampa Bay's biggest stars. Especially Junior Caminero. The Rays' star slugger had arguably his worst performance of the season against Cleveland, going 0-for-4 with four strikeou
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays are now facing a difficult situation in the American League Championship Series after falling 3-2 to the Cleveland Guardians in Game 3 on Thursday.
And while there are plenty of things to criticize about the performance, I think the biggest concern continues to be the lack of offensive production from Tampa Bay's biggest stars.
Especially Junior Caminero.
The Rays' star slugger had arguably his worst performance of the season against Cleveland, going 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.
And it wasn't necessarily because Gavin Williams was throwing pitches that were impossible to hit. Caminero consistently took hittable pitches early in counts before chasing balls well outside the strike zone.
That's something we haven't seen much of throughout the regular season. A year where he has surely earned votes for American League MVP.
And I think it's fair to wonder whether Caminero is trying to do too much at the plate.
The 45-home-run slugger still hasn't hit a home run this postseason, and his batting average sits at .238 with a .666 OPS.
Those numbers certainly aren't what Tampa Bay needs from one of its biggest offensive weapons.
But Caminero isn't the only player struggling.
Yandy Díaz is hitting .240 with a .589 OPS, while Jonathan Aranda has managed just a .182 batting average and .568 OPS.
Victor Mesa Jr. is hitting .143, and Liam Hicks isn't doing much better at .167.
These are supposed to be the players carrying Tampa Bay's offense.
Instead, the Rays have relied on contributions from the bottom of their lineup.
Chandler Simpson delivered Tampa Bay's only two runs Thursday with an impressive two-RBI triple against Williams.
Richie Palacios has also provided some important hits, while Jonny DeLuca has been one of Tampa Bay's more productive hitters throughout the series.
But that can't continue being the expectation.
Tampa Bay won 98 games during the regular season because it had a lineup capable of consistently putting the baseball in play and creating scoring opportunities.
However, the Rays have yet to score more than four runs in a postseason game.
And Thursday might've been the most frustrating example.
Tampa Bay managed just three hits and struck out 13 times, including seven strikeouts from the top of the batting order.
The Rays also went down in order in seven of their nine offensive innings.
That's not going to get the job done in October.
Especially against a Cleveland team that has consistently taken advantage of its opportunities.
Now, I'm not suggesting Tampa Bay's season is over.
The Rays are only trailing 2-1 in a seven-game series, and there's still plenty of baseball left to play.
But if Tampa Bay wants to reach the World Series, its biggest offensive stars need to start playing like it.
And that starts with Junior Caminero.

item.content:encoded:
New York radio host Tommy Lugauer has made a strong case for the New York Yankees to pursue San Diego Padres star Fernando Tatis Jr. in a blockbuster trade. Lugauer argued that the outfielder could address several of the team's roster concerns.
The Yankees' 2026 postseason campaign ended with a 3-0 sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series, extending their World Series drought to 17 seasons. New York entered the playoffs as the No. 4 seed after finishing the regular season with a 93-68 record, second in the AL East behind Tampa Bay.
Following the disappointing postseason exit, Lugauer discussed the Yankees' offseason priorities during a segment on WFAN Sports Radio. He argued that acquiring the $340 million star should be at the top of the team's list, praising the 27-year-old's offensive production, defensive ability, and potential fit in New York.
"The Yankees' top priority in the offseason should be doing everything in their power to acquire Fernando Tatis Jr. Tatis would solve a million issues for the Yankees. Leadoff hitter clutch, an electric player defensively, offensively. I think Fernando Tatis Junior would be a rock star in New York, a rock star. And he should be their future right fielder for the Yankees," said Lugauer.
He added:
"Judge is to either DH or first base, and or maybe a combination of both. Right field's going to be wide open, and who better to man right field for years to come with the Yankees than Tatis?"
Fernando Tatis last played in the 2026 postseason on October 7, when the Padres lost 3-1 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series, ending San Diego's season.
Fernando Tatis Jr. reflects on the Padres' 2026 season
After the San Diego Padres lost to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the NLDS and got eliminated from the playoffs, Fernando Tatis Jr. spoke to reporters about what he had learned throughout the season and his determination to keep improving.
The outfielder emphasized his commitment to growing both on and off the field, while continuing to work toward delivering the results San Diego's fans expect.
"It's a lot of learning experience. I was just gonna put it that way, you know, this game will teach you so many stuff on and off the field every single year, so at my disposal. Simple servant, I'm just here to keep learning every single year to keep getting better as a person, as a man. As a father, you know, and we're just gonna keep battling and find a way to give San Diego what they really deserve," said Tatis.
Fernando Tatis finished the 2026 regular season with 181 hits and 96 runs scored across 159 games, recording 626 at-bats.

item.title: [mlb.com] Who should Brewers want to face in the World Series?
item.dc:creator: Zach Sweet

item.content:encoded:
When the Brewers finished off the Dodgers on Thursday night, their World Series opponent was the last thing on anyone’s mind. An MLB official closed the postgame press conference by telling manager Pat Murphy and NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, “We’ll see you in Milwaukee at the World Series.”
Murphy’s reply said everything: “When’s that start?”
Next Friday, Oct. 23, at American Family Field, where Milwaukee holds home-field advantage thanks to its franchise-record 103 wins. The Guardians took a 2-1 ALCS lead over the Rays into Friday night's scheduled Game 4 at Progressive Field. Milwaukee, meanwhile, will have a full week to rest, which leaves plenty of time to watch and wonder.
Here’s a guide to each potential matchup. You decide which one you’d rather see.
If the regular season is a guide ...
It doesn’t tell us much. The Brewers went 2-1 against both teams.
Milwaukee won the first two games against Cleveland on June 16-17 before rookie left-hander Parker Messick struck out nine over six innings in the finale. Cleveland was without José Ramírez, Angel Martínez and Chase DeLauter. All three are back.
When the Brewers hit
Milwaukee’s lineup is built on pressure. The Brewers ranked in the top five in doubles, runs, hits, walks, batting average and on-base percentage.
That approach might get more of a test against Tampa Bay. The Rays issued the fewest walks in the Majors (409) and ranked second in defensive runs saved (87). Drawing walks and finding holes gets tougher against that combination. And their top starters have carried it into October: Drew Rasmussen has a 1.29 ERA through two postseason starts, while Peralta has allowed one earned run in 10 2/3 innings, including six shutout innings in Game 2 of the ALCS.
Cleveland offers a different challenge. Gavin Williams has been a monster, striking out 33 over 16 2/3 innings this postseason. The Guardians have a 2.54 ERA this October, slightly better than Tampa Bay’s 2.72. But Cleveland issued 530 regular-season walks to the Rays’ 409, giving Milwaukee more reason to believe its patient approach can create traffic.
When the other side hits
The regular-season numbers favor facing Cleveland. The Guardians had the lowest OPS (.696) and fewest runs (678) of any postseason team. Tampa Bay offered a more complete attack, with Junior Caminero’s 42 homers anchoring a lineup that tied for fifth in on-base percentage (.326).
October has told a different story. Through Thursday, Cleveland was averaging 4.25 runs per game with a .685 OPS, compared with Tampa Bay’s 3.00 runs and .563 OPS. The Guardians haven’t suddenly become an offensive powerhouse, but they’ve been more productive than the Rays, whose lineup managed just three hits in Game 3 of the ALCS.
The larger sample still points toward Cleveland as the preferable opponent. The way these teams are hitting right now makes that a tougher call.
The bullpens
Neither ninth inning looks inviting. Tampa Bay’s Bryan Baker has saved all four Rays wins this postseason without allowing a hit in four innings. Ian Seymour has been a strong bridge, allowing one earned run in 6 1/3 innings.
Cleveland counters with Cade Smith, who has allowed two hits and one run while striking out 13 in nine innings this October. Hunter Gaddis has added six scoreless innings across seven appearances. Both teams have arms capable of shortening games.
The Brewers have made a habit of coming back this postseason, and their bats have shown they can pick at a bullpen late. Against either opponent, getting a lead before the closer enters would make life easier.
What about the intangibles?
The Guardians’ championship drought dates to 1948. The Rays, like the Brewers, have never won a World Series.
The Rays mirror Milwaukee in many ways. Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold worked in Tampa Bay’s front office alongside current Rays GM Erik Neander. Add Peralta facing his former team, and the storyline writes itself.
Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt played for Milwaukee and interviewed for the job that went to Murphy three years ago. And a Cleveland-Milwaukee World Series comes with a built-in movie reference: Major League, filmed in Milwaukee with Bob Uecker’s Harry Doyle calling Cleveland's improbable run.
The verdict
Give the Guardians a slight edge as Milwaukee’s preferred opponent, though their October bats have made that a tougher sell. The Rays were the more complete team over six months. Cleveland has spent the past two weeks making those six months feel a little less relevant.
The Brewers? They just sent the back-to-back champs home. They’ll let the AL sort this out. Somebody remind Murph what time Friday’s game starts.

item.content:encoded:
Milwaukee Brewers superstar Jackson Chourio is the odds-on favorite to win the World Series MVP in the 2026 Fall Classic.
The Brewers advanced to the World Series for the first time since 1982, when they took down the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers, the reigning two-time World Series champions, with an eye-opening 4-0 sweep in the NLCS.
It was an absolutely incredible performance by the Brewers, who are now four wins away from capturing the first World Series championship in franchise history.
If they do end up winning it, then the oddsmakers like Chourio’s chances to be a big part of them doing so.
Jackson Chourio Is the World Series MVP Favorite
Per DraftKings Sportsbook, Chourio is the odds-on favorite to win the World Series MVP award this season.
Chourio is currently at +600 odds, putting him just ahead of his Brewers teammates, C William Contreras at +650, SP Jacob Misiorowski at +700, and 2B Brice Turang at +900, to capture this year’s World Series MVP award.
Since the ALCS between the Cleveland Guardians and the Tampa Bay Rays has not yet been decided, the odds will change from now until the start of the World Series one week from now.
Still, Chourio will be among the favorites to capture the World Series MVP award when the Brewers try to win the first championship in club history.
Jackson Chourio Is a Young Stud
Just 22 years old, Chourio is a young stud who has proven that he is one of the best young players in MLB since making his debut in 2024.
This season, Chourio hit .291 with a .837 OPS and a 129 OPS+ for the Brewers, indicating that his bat was 29% above league average.
He also belted 25 home runs and racked up 4.9 bWAR for the Brewers, along with stealing 23 bases.
Defensively, he had a strong year in LF and is a finalist for the Gold Glove Award.
During the postseason this year, Chourio has struggled a bit with just a .171 batting average, .553 OPS, and two home runs in eight games. But that is a very small sample size, and the oddsmakers know that he can turn it on at any moment.

item.title: [mlb.com] Mitchell keeps proving doubters wrong -- all the way to the World Series
item.dc:creator: Adam McCalvy
item.description: Ever since, there have been people who doubted that Mitchell could stay healthy enough, long enough, to handle the rigors of center field for a season that stretches 162 games, and, for the pennant-winning Brewers, well beyond. But he’s played more games this year than his first four years combined, and he was plenty healthy enough on Thursday night to deliver the tiebreaking solo home run that sent the Brewers from four runs down in the early innings to a victory and a trip to the World Series.
item.content:encoded:
Ever since, there have been people who doubted that Mitchell could stay healthy enough, long enough, to handle the rigors of center field for a season that stretches 162 games, and, for the pennant-winning Brewers, well beyond. But he’s played more games this year than his first four years combined, and he was plenty healthy enough on Thursday night to deliver the tiebreaking solo home run that sent the Brewers from four runs down in the early innings to a victory and a trip to the World Series.
“Growing up, he’s always one that his chip, his edge, his grit, was proving people wrong,” said Antony Mitchell, Garrett’s dad. “I told him, ‘It’s time to make the big shift.' That’s what he’s doing right now.”
Mitchell had two hits in the NLCS, a 4-0 Brewers sweep of the two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers. He made them count. In Game 3 on Wednesday, he followed Jake Bauers’ go-ahead, 11-pitch, two-run homer with a solo shot for the third set of back-to-back homers for left-handed hitters off a left-handed pitcher in postseason history. Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig were the first in 1928. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper were the second earlier this month.
A night later, Mitchell connected off a lefty again. The Brewers had trailed, 4-0, after slumping superstar Shohei Ohtani came to life with a three-run home run. No team had ever come back from a deficit that large to complete a postseason series sweep. Until these Brewers.
In the sixth, the Dodgers brought in a fresh left-handed reliever in Tanner Scott. He had not allowed a home run to a left-handed hitter all year, regular season and postseason. At the bat rack, right-handed hitter Andrew Vaughn stood ready to pinch-hit if called upon.
“I just heard an explosion go off,” Vaughn said. “The ball was crushed. What a sweet swing.”
Naturally, Mitchell said he was just trying to have a good at-bat, especially after falling behind, 0-2. He looked at three straight balls out of the strike zone, then got a fastball as center-cut as they come. Mitchell hit it out. The Brewers had the lead. For the sixth time in their seven victories in eight games so far this postseason, they came from behind to win.
“We’re savages, man,” Mitchell said. “We go down four runs early there, and nobody panics. This is what we’ve been doing. I’m just so proud of our team.”
Imagine how proud dad was, up in the stands. He could tell the game was slowing down for his son by the way he carried himself, pitch to pitch. And how proud the Brewers’ amateur scouting director, Tod Johnson, was feeling as he watched it unfold.
“I’ll be honest: He’s probably not a Brewer if he doesn’t have diabetes,” Johnson said. “He fell [to 20th overall] because of concerns about that. Then he battled through different injuries that are not necessarily related to that. But [before the Draft], we did a lot of work on it.”
It helped that Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold had history with Rays outfielder Sam Fuld, a diabetic and one of Mitchell’s role models as a young ballplayer.
“To do something like he did on this stage is a message for everybody that if you put your mind to it, you can do it,” Arnold said. “He’s overcome so much.”
They all know well what it took Mitchell to get to that moment. He wears a pod that delivers insulin and is connected to his cell phone, which Mitchell checks periodically throughout the day and during games. On several occasions this season, Mitchell’s blood sugar got out of whack and he had to miss games. With his increased workload, he had to train himself to eat more, and at the right times, to be available as often as possible.
Along the way, he has met many young diabetic kids playing sports, offering advice and support.
“He has managed himself for many years, and here he is, an example to kids that anything is possible,” Antony Mitchell said. “It’s a disease, and you have to learn to manage it. It’s not easy. He makes things look easy sometimes, but he works really hard to make it all work. These were special moments.
“He loves kids, he loves this game, he loves his team. Here they are, celebrating. We’re going to the World Series. This is so fantastic.”

Furthermore, OG operates within the US federally regulated framework for event contracts overseen by the CFTC, rather than under state sports-betting licenses.
Where Can You Trade With OG?
Trading is open to users who are 18 years or older and physically located in the United States.
Because OG operates under federal event-contract regulation, the exchange is available far more widely than traditional state-licensed sportsbooks. Access is still restricted in a small number of states where local regulators have challenged prediction markets.
Because this regulatory position is subject to ongoing legal challenges and can rapidly change, traders should confirm current availability directly in the OG app or on the OG site before signing up.
18+, US only, event-contract trading carries risk of loss, other terms and conditions may apply, trade responsibly.

item.content:encoded:
아이러니를 야구로 표현하면 이렇게 되지 않을까 싶다. 지난 10월 14일 현재 진행 중인 메이저리그 포스트시즌 챔피언십시리즈에서 내셔널리그는 초호화 스타군단 LA 다저스와 스몰마켓의 대명사 밀워키 브루어스가 맞붙었다. 아메리칸리그에서는 대표적 저연봉 구단인 탬파베이 레이스와 클리블랜드 가디언스가 월드시리즈 진출을 다투고 있다. 4개 팀 중 다저스를 제외한 3개 팀이 저연봉 구단이다. 연봉총액 순위에서 다저스는 약 3억3932만달러로 전체 2위인데 밀워키는 19위, 탬파베이는 28위, 클리블랜드는 최하위인 30위다. 다저스 한 팀의 연봉총액이 나머지 세 구단을 합친 금액보다 많다.
저연봉 팀들의 돌풍
공교롭게도 MLB 노사는 지금 샐러리캡 도입을 놓고 강대강 대치 중이다. 욕심 많은 구단주들이 야합해 ‘돈 많은 팀만 우승하는 구조를 바꾸자’며 연봉 상한제 도입을 밀어붙이고 있다.
그런데 정작 월드시리즈를 눈앞에 둔 팀들은 대부분 돈 없는 가난뱅이 구단들이다. 연봉총액 1위 뉴욕 메츠는 꼴찌로 추락해 가을야구에도 오르지 못했고, 부자 구단인 뉴욕 양키스와 보스턴 레드삭스, 시카고 컵스도 줄줄이 탈락했다. 심지어 다저스마저 밀워키와의 챔피언십시리즈 1, 2차전을 모두 내주며 벼랑 끝에 몰렸다. 만약 밀워키가 다저스를 꺾는다면 밀워키와 클리블랜드, 혹은 밀워키와 탬파베이의 월드시리즈가 성사된다. 이른바 ‘흥참시(흥행 참패 시리즈)’에 MLB 사무국과 중계 방송사들은 죽을 맛이겠지만, 샐러리캡 반대 진영에는 ‘거 봐라’라며 내세울 강력한 논리가 생긴다.
메이저리그 구단주들의 샐러리캡 도입 기도는 역사가 길다. 각 팀이 선수 연봉에 쓸 수 있는 돈의 상한선을 정해 부자 구단과 가난한 구단의 격차를 줄이겠다는 게 대외적인 취지. 이 그럴싸한 명분을 앞세운 구단주 연합은 1994년에도 샐러리캡 도입을 추진하다 선수노조와 정면충돌했다. 선수들의 파업으로 1994년 월드시리즈가 취소됐고, 이듬해 정규시즌도 단축됐다. 메이저리그 인기는 바닥을 쳤고, 다시 인기를 되찾는 데는 많은 시간과 다량의 금지약물이 필요했다.
오는 12월 기존 노사협약(CBA) 만료를 앞두고는 ‘신 악의 제국’ 다저스 논란이 샐러리캡 도입론에 다시 불을 붙였다. 다저스는 오타니 쇼헤이, 무키 베츠, 프레디 프리먼, 야마모토 요시노부 등 스타들을 끌어모아 2024년과 2025년 월드시리즈를 제패했다. 압도적 자금력으로 최고 선수들을 쓸어담는 다저스 때문에 리그의 경쟁균형이 무너졌다는 게 샐러리캡을 염불처럼 외는 구단주들의 논리다. MLB 사무국은 올해 노사협상에서 2027년부터 팀당 연봉총액 상한선 2억4530만달러, 하한선 1억7120만달러를 적용하는 방안을 제시했다.
하지만 구단주들의 논리가 설득력이 떨어진다는 비판도 만만치 않다. 스포츠매체 디애슬레틱의 켄 로젠탈 선임기자는 밀워키와 클리블랜드, 탬파베이 같은 저연봉 구단들이 꾸준히 좋은 성적을 거두는 사실을 지적하며, 샐러리캡을 시행하는 미 프로풋볼(NFL)과 미 프로농구(NBA)에서도 특정 구단의 장기 집권과 우승 독식이 반복된다고 꼬집었다. 샐러리캡이 반드시 공정한 경쟁을 보장하지는 않는다는 얘기다. 구단 간 수익 배분을 개선하고 돈 안 쓰는 구단주들의 투자를 유도하는 방식을 대안으로 제시한 로젠탈은 구단주들을 향해 “다른 방법으로 야구를 개선하라. 아니면 팀을 팔아버려라”라고 쏘아붙였다.
구단주들은 야구를 개선하거나 팀을 팔 생각도, 샐러리캡을 포기할 생각도 없어 보인다. 경쟁균형은 명분일 뿐, 진짜 목적은 선수 연봉 지출을 줄여 더 많은 돈을 쓸어담는 데 있으니 다른 건 다 내줘도 샐러리캡만은 포기 못 한다.
내년 직장폐쇄 가능성 커
현행 CBA는 미국 동부 기준 오는 12월 1일 만료된다. 새 협약에 합의하지 못하면 구단주들은 직장폐쇄에 돌입할 전망이다. 그러면 2027시즌도 파행을 피하기 어려워진다. 2021년 12월엔 직장폐쇄 99일 만에 새 협약을 체결해 정규시즌을 무사히 치렀지만, 이번에는 샐러리캡이라는 뇌관이 있어 쉽게 풀릴 것 같지 않다. 협상이 길어지면 개막이 늦어지고, 더 길어지면 아예 경기 수가 줄어들 수 있다. 구단주들은 60경기 이상 취소되는 걸 ‘파국’으로 간주한다. 최악의 경우 2027시즌 전체가 날아가는 ‘파멸’이 기다린다. 어쩌면 지금 진행 중인 포스트시즌이 당분간 우리가 볼 마지막 메이저리그 경기가 될지도 모른다.
MLB 사무국은 이미 파멸을 대비하는 분위기다. 디애슬레틱이 입수한 내부 문건에 따르면 사무국은 구단과 리그 관계자들에게 직장폐쇄 대비 지침을 전달했다. 선수들의 구단 시설 이용과 구단 직원의 업무상 연락을 금지하고, 크리스마스 카드나 연말 선물을 보내는 것까지 막는다는 내용이다. 공식 홈페이지에서도 선수들의 사진과 영상이 사라진다. MLB는 2027시즌 경기 취소에 대비해 시즌권 구매자에게 환불이나 적립금을 제공하는 방안까지 마련했다. 최악의 상황도 불사하겠다는 의지가 느껴진다.
메이저리그의 직장폐쇄는 태평양 건너 한국야구에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 야구의 세계화 시대에 미국야구에서 벌어지는 일은 더 이상 딴나라 남의 이야기가 아니다. 우선 KBO리그 외국인 선수 수급에 큰 변수가 생길 수 있다. SSG 랜더스의 외국인 투수 페드로 아빌라 사례를 보자. 아빌라는 지난 7월 대체 외국인 선수로 합류해 14경기에서 9승 2패, 평균자책 1.44라는 놀라운 성적을 남겼다. 93.2이닝 동안 삼진 93개를 잡고 두 차례 완투까지 기록하며 SSG 선발진을 이끌었다. 경기 수가 적어서 그렇지 풀시즌 기준으로는 에릭 페디, 코디 폰세급 활약이다.
이 정도 성적이라면 당연히 메이저리그 복귀를 노려볼 만하다. 실제 여러 빅리그 구단이 아빌라를 영입 후보에 올려놓고 관찰해 왔다. 페디, 폰세처럼 거액을 받고 메이저리그로 금의환향하는 게 일반적인 수순이다. 하지만 올해는 다르다. 내년 시즌이 정상적으로 열릴지 불확실한데 자칫 미국행을 택했다가 한 시즌을 통째로 날릴 수도 있다. 아빌라도 이런 사정을 고려해 KBO리그 잔류 쪽으로 기우는 분위기다. 같은 이유에서 지난해까지 한화 이글스에서 뛰었던 라이언 와이스도 한국 복귀를 원하는 것으로 전해졌다.
오타니의 일본 리그 복귀?
한 구단 관계자는 “올겨울 팀들의 외국인 선수 구성이 예년보다 느리게 진행될 것”이라며 “다들 메이저리그 상황을 지켜보며 서두르지 않으려는 분위기”라고 전했다. 예년에는 기존 선수와 재계약도 새 선수 영입도 빠르게 진행하는 게 유리했다면 올해는 기다리는 편이 나을 수 있다. 노사협상이 길어질수록 평소 한국행을 꿈에도 생각하지 않았던 선수들이 시장에 나올 가능성이 있어서다. 빅리그 승격이나 단기 계약을 노리는 선수들로서는 언제 기회가 올지 알 수 없으니, 차라리 한 시즌 계약과 꾸준한 출전이 보장되고 MLB 스카우트들이 매 경기를 지켜보는 KBO리그가 나을 수 있다. 국내 구단들로선 지금까지 ‘감히’ 영입 제안을 건네기 어려웠던 선수들에게도 접근할 기회가 생긴다. 애매한 선수와 섣불리 계약했다간 나중에 후회되는 상황이 생길지도 모른다.
좀 더 극단적인 상황도 상상할 수 있다. 직장폐쇄가 장기화해 2027시즌 MLB가 아예 열리지 않는다면 어떻게 될까. 미국에서 뛰던 정상급 선수들이 한국이나 일본 프로야구에서 한 시즌을 보내는 상황도 생각해 볼 수 있다. 놀랍게도 MLB는 이를 막지 않겠다는 방침이다. 디애슬레틱이 공개한 MLB 문건에는 직장폐쇄 기간 선수들의 다른 프로리그 출전을 제한하지 않겠다는 내용이 담겼다. 일본 프로야구와 윈터리그를 비롯한 국외 프로리그가 대상이니, 당연히 한국도 포함된다.
그렇다면 오타니 쇼헤이, 애런 저지, 폴 스킨스, 타릭 스쿠벌 같은 슈퍼스타들이 한국이나 일본에서 뛰는 일도 가능할까. 이론적으로는 가능한 시나리오다. 애런 저지가 롯데 자이언츠 유니폼을 입고 사직구장 타석에 나오고, 게릿 콜이 한화 이글스 유니폼을 입고 대전 마운드에 오르는, AI 합성물로나 만들 법한 장면을 상상하는 걸 멈추기 어렵다. 물론 한국 구단이 감당하기 어려운 몸값부터 기존 계약과 리그 규약까지 넘어야 할 산이 많아 실현 가능성은 희박해도 팬들로서는 해볼 법한 행복한 상상이다.
MLB 직장폐쇄는 한국인 빅리거들의 진로에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 특히 올 시즌을 끝으로 애틀랜타 브레이브스와 계약이 끝난 김하성에게는 민감한 문제다. 김하성은 지난해 12월 애틀랜타와 1년 2000만달러에 계약했다. 올해 좋은 성적으로 FA 대박 계약을 따내겠다는 구상이었지만 기대에 크게 못 미쳤다. 올해 성적으로는 장기 계약은커녕 마이너리그 계약을 걱정해야 한다는 게 현지 평가. 여기에 내년 시즌의 정상 개최 여부도 불확실해 김하성이 한시적인 국내 복귀를 고려할 수 있다는 전망도 조금씩 나온다. 미국에서 언제 될지 모르는 계약을 기다리느니 한국에서 한 시즌을 뛰며 경기 감각을 되찾고, 상황이 정리된 뒤 메이저리그에 재도전한다는 시나리오다. 이 경우 원소속팀 키움 히어로즈가 우선적인 권리를 갖는다.
키움 우승후보 될 수도
여기서 상상력을 더 발휘하면 정말 흥미로운 그림이 나온다. 현재 미국에서 뛰는 이정후·김혜성·송성문의 KBO리그 일시 복귀 가능성이다. 만약 직장폐쇄가 장기화하고 MLB 구단과 계약한 선수들의 한국 리그 일시 출전까지 허용된다면 어떨까. KBO가 특수한 상황을 고려해 한국인 메이저리거의 원소속팀 한시 복귀를 허용하는 특별 규정까지 마련한다면, 김하성·이정후·김혜성·송성문이 내년 시즌 키움에서 다시 뭉치는 상황도 생각해 볼 수 있다. 4년 연속 최하위에 머문 키움이 하루아침에 우승후보가 되는 상황이다.
물론 가정에 가정을 더하고 상상에 상상을 더해야 가능한 이야기다. 하지만 메이저리그가 실제 직장폐쇄에 돌입하고 2027시즌마저 날아가는, 아무도 가보지 않은 길에 접어든다면 무슨 일이 생길지 모른다. 미국의 야구가 멈추는 순간, 한국야구에도 지금까지 경험하지 못한 일들이 벌어질 수 있다. 올 초 기자에게 “직장폐쇄 가능성이 50 대 50”이라고 했던 미국 구단 관계자는 최근 다시 물었을 때 “90%”라고 답했다.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Latest Dodgers Prediction Gives Tigers Hope for a Tarik Skubal Reunion
item.dc:creator: Alvin Garcia; Unknown
item.description: The Detroit Tigers have another reason to consider bringing Tarik Skubal home as questions grow about his future with the Los Angeles Dodgers. In ESPN’s offseason outlook, Alden Gonzalez predicts no massive Skubal extension with the Dodgers before Dec. 1. His forecast centers on uncertainty over MLB’s next economic system as the collective bargaining agreement approaches expiration and a potential lockout looms. item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Tigers have another reason to consider bringing Tarik Skubal home as questions grow about his future with the Los Angeles Dodgers.
In ESPN’s offseason outlook, Alden Gonzalez predicts no massive Skubal extension with the Dodgers before Dec. 1.
His forecast centers on uncertainty over MLB’s next economic system as the collective bargaining agreement approaches expiration and a potential lockout looms. It is a prediction about timing, not a confirmed decision that Los Angeles will never offer Skubal a contract.
For the Tigers, that creates a possibility worth exploring. A cautious bidder could leave room for Detroit to act, particularly if Skubal wants his future settled before a work stoppage.
The available evidence supports a plausible reunion. Making it happen still requires an offer competitive enough to overcome the rest of the market.
Why a Skubal Reunion Remains Realistic
Skubal has already supplied the strongest personal reason to take the possibility seriously.
"I would love to return," he said during an August appearance on Pardon My Take, as Tigers On SI covered when examining his free-agency hopes.
Those comments came after Detroit traded him to Los Angeles. The separation clearly did not eliminate his interest in the organization where he developed into a two-time American League Cy Young Award winner.
A return would also give the Tigers an appealing outcome: bringing back their former ace while retaining the players acquired in the trade. That would strengthen the rotation without requiring another prospect package.
The market assessment comes with a qualification, however. In his Oct. 2 survey of industry insiders, ESPN’s Kiley McDaniel included Detroit among possible contenders alongside the Dodgers and New York Mets. He also noted that insiders more often viewed the Tigers as being on the periphery.
That distinction matters when assessing their actual chances. There is a credible connection between the player and the team, but the public reporting provides little basis for treating Detroit as the favorite.
Skubal’s willingness to return gives the front office a reason to engage. It does not establish that he will accept less money to do so.
Detroit’s Biggest Hurdle Is the Financial Commitment
McDaniel’s 27 contract projections averaged eight years and $355 million. That is an industry forecast rather than a reported asking price, but it illustrates the scale of the potential commitment.
The Tigers have demonstrated a willingness to invest in starting pitching. Their three-year, $115 million agreement with Framber Valdez represents a substantial expenditure. A deal approaching Skubal’s projected guarantee would require a much longer commitment and more than three times that total.
There is also a broader roster to build. President of baseball operations Scott Harris has described free agency as a way to supplement Detroit’s developing core. A Skubal pursuit would test how aggressively ownership is willing to fund that approach while leaving resources for additional improvements.
The labor uncertainty affecting Los Angeles also applies to Detroit. The Tigers cannot assume that waiting for new economic rules will produce a cheaper ace, or that other bidders will remain cautious.
Their clearest path is a competitive offer early enough to matter. If Detroit authorizes a guarantee near the market’s upper end, Skubal’s affection for the city gives the club something meaningful to build on.
If the plan depends on a substantial hometown discount, the Dodgers’ hesitation offers limited help.
A reunion deserves serious consideration. Detroit’s chances ultimately depend on whether its financial commitment matches its former ace’s interest in coming back.
Alvin Garcia is a Puerto Rico-born sportswriter and U.S. Army veteran. He has covered Major League Baseball since 2022, producing breaking news, game coverage, analysis, roster stories and player features for national and team-focused publications. His previous work has appeared at Heavy, The Sporting News, Athlon Sports, Yardbarker, and FanSided. Garcia brings a data-informed, fan-focused approach to his coverage.

item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees saw their playoff lives come crashing down in the American League Division Series to the Tampa Bay Rays.
After sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the wild-card series, New York was swept by Tampa Bay. This now sends the Yankees into a tough offseason, filled with all sorts of questions around the organization.
New York did play the series against Tampa Bay without star Aaron Judge due to injury, giving the team some leeway. But the early postseason exit just marks another season where the Yankees didn't win the World Series.
And as the team enters the offseason, the front office has a lot of work to do to fix the roster. The starting pitching was the strength of this team all season, but the Yankees could elect to keep diving into it.
One name that could make some sense for New York to go after is ace Tarik Skubal, who split time between the Detroit Tigers and Los Angeles Dodgers this year. Skubal is seen by many as one of the best pitchers in baseball, and he will be hitting free agency this offseason.
MLB analyst Zachary D. Rymer of Bleacher Report linked the Yankees to Skubal, listing them as a top landing spot. New York is one of the few teams across baseball that may be willing to give the lefty ace the type of contract that he desires in free agency.
Many are expecting Skubal to receive over $300 million in free agency, but whether the Yankees would e willing to pay this remains to be seen. Skubal could add to a rotation that has Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon, giving New York the best group in baseball.
Cole is getting older and he wasn't as effective this year, so the Skubal argument could make sense. The left-hander was very good again this season, even with him missing time due to an injury.
Skubal posted a 2.72 ERA over 26 starts between the two teams, while striking out 186 batters over 158.2 innings. The left-hander remained dominant on the mound, and he has more than earned a massive payday this offseason.
New York could be a solid landing spot for Skubal, giving him the chance to play in the biggest city that the sport has to offer. But the Yankees will have competition to sign Skubal this offseason, which could see a bidding war take place.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] New York Mets Get Great Tarik Skubal Update Before MLB Free Agency
item.dc:creator: Michael DeRosa
item.description: The New York Mets are going to be one of baseball's most fascinating teams to watch this offseason. After underperforming in such a significant way this season, the expectation is that the Mets will be very active in free agency. It is understandable, as they want to be contenders and have a lot of work to do with their roster to become that. One of the biggest rumors surrounding the Mets is their expected pursuit of Los Angeles Dodgers superstar pitcher Tarik Skubal. It is very easy to understa
item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets are going to be one of baseball's most fascinating teams to watch this offseason.
After underperforming in such a significant way this season, the expectation is that the Mets will be very active in free agency. It is understandable, as they want to be contenders and have a lot of work to do with their roster to become that.
One of the biggest rumors surrounding the Mets is their expected pursuit of Los Angeles Dodgers superstar pitcher Tarik Skubal. It is very easy to understand why New York is being linked to him. They desperately need pitching help, and Skubal is baseball's best pitcher. Thus, the Mets making a major push for him this offseason simply makes sense.
Now, with the Dodgers getting swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the Mets have gotten a very good prediction regarding the Skubal sweepstakes.
New York Mets Get Great Tarik Skubal Update Before MLB Free Agency
In a recent Bleacher Report article, Zachary D. Rymer named the Mets as the "top contender" to land Skubal this offseason in free agency.
"The Mets are the top contender for Skubal because of course they are. Steve Cohen may not be MLB's richest owner anymore, but his track record speaks for itself," Rymer wrote.
"Under him, the Mets have had MLB's No. 1 Opening Day payroll in three of the last four years. And while president of baseball operations David Stearns clearly falls on the risk-averse side, Cohen has been known to put his finger on the scale until it climbs all the way to $765 million. That was for Juan Soto, of course, and there's no denying that the Mets need his equal on the mound. Their starting rotation was a disaster this year, ranking 23rd in ERA and rWAR," Rymer added.
Seeing the Mets be named the most likely team to land Skubal right now is certainly encouraging. It is also understandable, as they are in desperate need of a true superstar pitcher. Due to this and New York's desperation to be contenders, it would not be shocking if they make a major push for Skubal this offseason.
Mets Landing Skubal Could Be Game-Changing
If the Mets landed Skubal this offseason, it could be game-changing. He is baseball's top pitcher and would significantly improve New York's starting rotation. This would undoubtedly help the Mets' chances of being a playoff team again next offseason because of it.
Skubal is a two-time Cy Young Award winner who was once again great this season. In 26 games in 2026, he had a 12-7 record, a 2.72 ERA, and 186 strikeouts. This marked the fourth season in a row that he had a 2.80 ERA or lower. With this, he would be a spectacular pickup for the Mets if brought in.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.content:encoded:
La tensión ha alcanzado su punto más alto en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana (ALCS). Tras tres intensos compromisos repletos de emociones, dramatismo y béisbol del más alto nivel, los Cleveland Guardians se colocaron a una sola victoria de conquistar el gallardete del joven circuito e instalarse en la Serie Mundial 2026. Por su parte, los Tampa Bay Rays afrontan este crucial Juego 4 sin margen de error, obligados a ganar para mantener con vida sus aspiraciones y forzar la extensión del compromiso.
La novena de Cleveland, que firmó una postemporada memorable tras venir de atrás en las rondas previas, se presenta a este cuarto capítulo con el viento a su favor y la posibilidad de terminar la obra en casa.
Sin embargo, enfrente tienen a una escuadra de Tampa Bay caracterizada por su resiliencia y capacidad estratégica para levantarse en momentos de máxima exigencia. Todo está servido para una batalla campal sobre el diamante en la que un error podría definir el destino de toda una campaña.
Así se han vivido los primeros tres partidos de la ALCS
El camino hacia este Juego 4 ha estado marcado por finales apretados y giros de tuerca constantes que han mantenido a la afición al borde del asiento.
Juego 1: golpe de autoridad visitante de Cleveland
El primer enfrentamiento de la serie en el Tropicana Field arrancó con un duelo táctico desde el montículo. Los Guardians lograron romper el cero en la quinta entrada gracias a la oportunidad de su parte baja del orden al bate. Pese a una tardía reacción de las mantarrayas en los episodios finales, el cerrador de Cleveland bajó la cortina para asegurar el triunfo por pizarra de 3-2, arrebatándole de inmediato la ventaja de localía a Tampa Bay.
Juego 2: dominio absoluto del pitcheo abridor
Para el segundo capítulo de la contienda, la rotación de los Guardians volvió a dar una lección de efectividad. Maniatando por completo a los maderos estelares de los Rays, el abridor de Cleveland trabajó seis entradas completas sin permitir anotación, recetando ocho ponches. Con un rally de tres carreras impulsado por extrabases consecutivos en la séptima entrada, Cleveland se impuso 4-1, poniendo la serie 2-0 a su favor y dejando desorientada a la escuadra floridana antes de viajar a Ohio.
Juego 3: La respuesta de orgullo y poder de Tampa Bay
Obligados a responder para no quedar al borde del abismo en suelo ajeno, los Rays mostraron su mejor versión en el tercer compromiso. Con un ataque agresivo desde el primer inning que incluyó un cuadrangular con hombres en base, la ofensiva de Tampa Bay descifró los lanzamientos del abridor rival. Aunque Cleveland intentó acortar distancias en el tramo final del juego, el relevo de las mantarrayas aguantó el embate para sellar el triunfo 6-4, recortando la diferencia en la serie (2-1) y extendiendo el duelo a un cuarto capítulo obligado.
El impacto de Jonathan Aranda: Los números del mexicano en la Serie de Campeonato
En medio de la intensa contienda por el banderín de la Liga Americana, la figura del infielder mexicano Jonathan Aranda ha destacado de forma sobresaliente en el line-up de los Tampa Bay Rays, consolidándose como uno de los bateadores más consistentes y oportunos del equipo durante esta fase de playoffs.
El tijuanaense ha asumido la responsabilidad de encabezar la ofensiva de su escuadra en los momentos de mayor presión. A lo largo de los primeros tres encuentros de la Serie de Campeonato, Aranda presume registros individuales de alto impacto:
- Promedio de Bateo (AVG): .364 en la serie (4 imparables en 11 turnos oficiales al bate).
- Cuadrangulares: 1 jonrón clave conectado durante el Juego 3 que inició la remontada de los Rays.
- Carreras Producidas: 3 carreras impulsadas, manteniéndose como el líder del equipo en este rubro durante la ALCS.
- Porcentaje de Embasado (OBP): .462, producto de su paciencia en la caja de bateo tras negociar dos pasaportes vitales.
La disciplina de Aranda frente a los lanzadores de Cleveland ha sido determinante para dar vueltas a la alineación y generar oportunidades de anotación. De cara al Juego 4, la aportación ofensiva del toletero mexicano será indispensable si Tampa Bay pretende descifrar el pitcheo rival y empatar la serie.
¿Cuándo, a qué hora y dónde ver en vivo desde México el Juego 4?
El cuarto duelo de esta vibrante Serie de Campeonato entre Cleveland Guardians y Tampa Bay Rays se jugará este viernes y contará con cobertura televisiva y digital completa para los aficionados en territorio mexicano.
A continuación, los datos confirmedos para dar seguimiento en vivo al encuentro:
- Fecha: Viernes 16 de octubre de 2026.
- Horario (Tiempo del Centro de México): 18:08 horas.
- Sede: Progressive Field, Cleveland, Ohio.
- Transmisión por Televisión (México): El partido se transmitirá en directo por televisión de paga a través de las señales de ESPN y Fox Sports México.
- Transmisión por Streaming: Disponible en plataformas digitales mediante Disney+ (sección de Deportes) y la aplicación de Fox Sports, así como a través del servicio oficial MLB.TV para los suscriptores de la liga.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Boston Red Sox Starter Nominated for Players’ Choice Award
item.dc:creator: Zach Coe

When the Boston Red Sox acquired Sonny Gray in an offseason deal with the St. Louis Cardinals, they were met with plenty of skepticism about whether or not the 36-year-old veteran could pitch in a big market like Boston after struggling during his time in New York as a member of the Yankees, and whether he could recapture his front-of-the-rotation form this late in his career. item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray impressed in his first, and maybe only, season in Boston.
When the Boston Red Sox acquired Sonny Gray in an offseason deal with the St. Louis Cardinals, they were met with plenty of skepticism about whether or not the 36-year-old veteran could pitch in a big market like Boston after struggling during his time in New York as a member of the Yankees, and whether he could recapture his front-of-the-rotation form this late in his career. Those two questions he answered emphatically, posting one of the best seasons of his career.
In 29 starts for Boston, Gray posted a 2.72 ERA, the fifth-lowest among qualified American League starters and the eighth-lowest among qualified starters in baseball. In addition to posting the second-lowest ERA of his career, Gray finished the season tied for the league lead in wins with 18. Gray’s career renaissance was especially important in 2026, as the Red Sox lost 2025 American League Cy Young Award runner-up Garrett Crochet to a left shoulder injury on April 26, which ended his regular season. In Crochet’s absence, Gray and rookie Payton Tolle helped carry the Red Sox pitching staff to the third-lowest team ERA in baseball.
As a result of his career renaissance season, Gray has earned a nod of respect from his peers, being named one of the three finalists for the American League’s Most Outstanding Pitcher at the MLB Players’ Choice Awards. Gray is joined by New York Yankees starter Cam Schlittler and Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease. No surprises among the trio named finalists, as they could very well be the same three named finalists for the American League Cy Young Award.
After putting his name on the map with a dominant Game 3 performance against the Red Sox in the 2025 Wild Card series, Schlittler’s second act was somehow better than his postseason performance. In 33 starts for New York, the Walpole, Mass. native posted a 1.95 ERA, the lowest among all qualified American League starters and second-lowest among all qualified starters in the sport. His spectacular sophomore season is likely to earn him the AL Cy Young Award.
Cease posted an almost equally impressive first season in Toronto. In 29 starts, the 30-year-old right-hander posted a 2.40 ERA, trailing only Schlittler in the American League, and the fourth-lowest mark among all qualified starters in the sport. Cease also continued his run as one of the most prolific strikeout pitchers in the sport, punching out 12.73 batters per nine innings, leading the American League and trailing only Milwaukee Brewers ace and likely National League Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski for the league lead.
The MLB Players' Choice Award winners will be announced during the week of Oct. 26.
Of note
With the Red Sox officially in offseason mode, Zach Coe and David Azer are back on the 'Entering Kenmore' Podcast discussing how close Boston is to winning a World Series, offseason needs, and whether or not the 2026 season was successful. Check it out wherever you get your podcasts, or in the YouTube player below:
